en.title: Google agrees to privacy safeguards in Spirit Airlines data deal
en.summary: Google has agreed to exclude employee medical files, disciplinary records and safety reports from its proposed $10 million purchase of Spirit Airlines' internal data, prompting unions to withdraw objections ahead of a November 17 bankruptcy court hearing.
body: Google has agreed to keep employee medical files, disciplinary records and safety reports out of its proposed purchase of Spirit Airlines' internal data, prompting unions representing former Spirit employees to withdraw their objections ahead of a bankruptcy court hearing in New York on November 17, 2026. Google bid $10 million for the records at an August 14 auction, as Spirit sold off assets after it stopped flying in May. Google intends to use the data to train artificial intelligence models.

The material Spirit originally offered included decades of company emails, employee training and travel records, and messages staff exchanged on Microsoft Teams. The Association of Flight Attendants-CWA challenged the sale four days after the auction, arguing that the proposed terms focused on removing information that could identify a customer even though much of what Google stood to acquire documented the working lives of Spirit employees. The machinists' union and Transport Workers Union Local 570 joined the objection.

Spirit's pilots raised a separate concern about information shared in confidence. In a court filing, the Air Line Pilots Association cited reports submitted through FAA-approved safety programs, and suggested pilots at other airlines could become less willing to report an incident if they believed a future buyer might obtain the report and identify the pilot who filed it.

Under the revised terms, Spirit would hire Tonic AI to strip identifying information from the records Google would receive, with an independent reviewer chosen in consultation with the unions checking that work. Google also agreed to keep the data confidential and refrain from trying to identify individuals, the flight attendants' union said on November 10. The exclusions also cover employee identification documents and drug and alcohol testing records. The bankruptcy judge still needs to approve the sale.

zh.title: Google收購精神航空內部資料案讓步：排除員工醫療與安全報告、工會撤回異議
zh.summary: Google同意將員工醫療檔案、懲戒紀錄與安全報告排除在其收購精神航空內部資料的計畫之外，工會因此撤回異議；此案將於11月17日由紐約破產法院審理。
body: Google同意將員工醫療檔案、懲戒紀錄與安全報告排除在其收購精神航空內部資料的計畫之外，代表前精神航空員工的工會因此撤回異議；紐約破產法院將於2026年11月17日審理此案。Google在8月14日的拍賣會上以1000萬美元出價競標這批資料，當時精神航空已於5月停飛、正在出售資產。Google打算用這些資料訓練人工智慧模型。
精神航空原本提供的資料包括數十年的公司電子郵件、員工訓練與差旅紀錄，以及員工在Microsoft Teams上往來的訊息。空服員協會（AFA-CWA）在拍賣四天後提出異議，主張原方案只著重移除可識別顧客的資訊，但Google將取得的資料多半記錄的是精神航空員工的工作生活。機械工會與運輸工人工會第570分會也加入異議。

精神航空的飛行員另有不同疑慮：美國航空飛行員協會（ALPA）在法院文件中提到，飛行員透過美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）核准的安全通報計畫提交的報告也可能落入買家手中；工會認為，若其他航空公司的飛行員擔心未來買家取得報告並辨識出通報者，可能不再願意通報事件。依修訂後條件，精神航空將聘請Tonic AI去除Google取得資料中的可識別資訊，並由與工會協商選出的獨立審查者查核。空服員協會表示，Google也同意對資料保密、不嘗試辨識個人。排除範圍還包括員工身分文件與藥物及酒精檢測紀錄。本案仍待破產法官核准。
